INEBILIZUMAB IS IN SUBPROTOCOL A ONLY, AND SUBPROTOCOL A IS LUPUS NEPHRITIS. NCT06570798 is 'A Phase 2, Open Label, Multicenter, Platform Trial to Assess the Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of Inebilizumab and Blinatumomab in Subjects With Autoimmune Diseases' (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, read 2026-11-14). Inebilizumab is given in Subprotocol A, systemic lupus erythematosus WITH nephritis; blinatumomab, a different asset, takes Subprotocol B (lupus with or without nephritis) and Subprotocol C (rheumatoid arthritis). Subprotocol A requires 'biopsy-proven, proliferative LN demonstrating class III or class IV' disease, SLEDAI-2K >= 6, and 'inadequate response, loss of response or intolerance to at least 1 therapy'. Two shares. (1) The lupus nephritis share of the SLE pool, taken from the book's own two lupus rows so they cannot disagree: data/epidemiology.csv carries Lupus Nephritis at 72,458 against Lupus Erythematosus, Systemic at 204,295, which is 0.354697 ('derived from the CDC lupus registry prevalence and the registries' own proportion developing nephritis, which is about 35% of systemic lupus patients'). (2) The proliferative share, class III plus class IV, the cut azn_saphnelo.csv makes for exactly this population: Gasparotto M, Gatto M, Binda V, Doria A, Moroni G, 'Lupus nephritis: clinical presentations and outcomes in the 21st century', Rheumatology (Oxford) 2020;59(Suppl 5):v39-v51 (doi 10.1093/rheumatology/keaa381, PMID 33280015), on the distribution of histological classes over 45 years: 'class IV accounting for 50%, class III for 25% and class V for 20%', so 0.75. 0.354697 x 0.75 = 0.266023, about 54,344 patients - the same 54,344 azn_saphnelo.csv's lupus nephritis layer reaches, by construction
column12: THE 'INADEQUATE RESPONSE TO AT LEAST 1 THERAPY' CRITERION IS NOT CUT HERE, on purpose, and azn_saphnelo.csv gives the reason in its own words: the row 'narrows to biopsy class and not to disease activity as well: the prevalent pool is the population that has active proliferative disease at some point, and cutting twice would count the same narrowing in both rows'. The same logic applies to prior-therapy failure, since essentially every prevalent biopsy-proven class III/IV patient has had at least one therapy. Against that, legn_lucar_g79d_t_cells.csv and nvs_rapcabtagene_autoleucel.csv do cut a refractory funnel at 0.151216 for a two-line-failure criterion; Subprotocol A asks for one line, not two, so that share is too tight here. column12: A JUDGEMENT WEARING A MEASUREMENT'S CLOTHES, and both directions are real. Too high: inebilizumab arrives into a lupus nephritis setting that already has two labelled add-ons, belimumab and voclosporin, where adult SLE has only belimumab; NCT06570798 is Phase 2 and open-label with no control arm on Subprotocol A, whose primary outcome is 'Treatment-emergent adverse events and serious adverse events through Week 52', not efficacy; and the denominator of the 4.30% anchor is the whole SLE pool, not an eligible subset. Too low: an anti-CD19 B-cell depleter in biopsy-proven proliferative disease that has already failed a line is a different order of intervention from an interferon-receptor blocker in general lupus, and the unmet need is at its highest exactly there
